correctness.rationale: Every arrow in the edge-union DAG strictly raises a level because a length-k walk would realize a forbidden nonzero product. The finite chain decomposition and exponential formula are bijective. The exact x,y coefficient is a nonnegative polynomial in F0,F1,F2 and (a)_d(b)_d/d!; the latter is monotone under (a,b)->(a-1,b+1) when a>=b+2, term by term, proving domination. The one-edge coefficient sum_{i<j}a_i a_j strictly increases under smoothing, and cardinality strictness handles proper subsets. Verified 251 brute profile cells and 18196 coefficient comparisons using the embedded verifier; those experiments are not the unrestricted proof.

originality.rationale: The 2005 structural classification and partial-injection chain distributions are credited. An earlier own full rank-polynomial optimum for k>=3 gives only the merged coefficient sum after u_j=t^(j-1), so it cannot imply separate counts of types having the same rank (for example rank 2 types (2,2,0) and (3,0,1) when n=6,k=3). The new assertion is complete typewise dominance with a separate two-variable smoothing argument and sharp equality. No equivalent implication was identified in inspected relevant primary sections or published database queries, though uninspected older sources or implicit stronger variants remain priority risks.

value.rationale: For nilpotent partial injections, the path-length partition is a complete natural cycle-free conjugacy-class invariant and determines all power ranks, while rank alone merges genuinely different types. The theorem optimizes every individual such conjugacy stratum simultaneously across all bounded-class nilpotent subsemigroups and gives explicit exact counts and sharp equality cases for all dimensions. The n=6, k=3 rank-2 example separates two types and demonstrates substance beyond a mere rank-total restatement.
